newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Egyptian envoy to meet Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian envoy to meet Netanyahu.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said an Egyptian envoy would brief him on Thursday on talks the envoy had with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to revive Middle East peacemaking.

"I haven't received a detailed report as yet from Osama al-Baz on his discussions yesterday in Gaza. I will hear him today. He will come this afternoon to deliver his impressions," Netanyahu told Israel Radio.
After meeting al-Baz in Gaza on Wednesday, Arafat said there was as yet no prospect of a summit with Netanyahu to break a two-month-old peace deadlock.
Netanyahu's groundbreaking in March on a Jerusalem settlement, known as Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic, brought peace talks to a standstill.
A halt to Jewish settlement expansion, including in Arab East Jerusalem, is Arafat's condition for resuming talks with Israel but Netanyahu rules it out.

The Israeli and Egyptian leaders, their countries partners to a 1979 treaty, said their summit on Tuesday in the Egyptian resort of Sharm el-Sheikh would be followed by more talks on ending the crisis.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said after meeting Netanyahu he hoped soon to bring the Palestinian leader into a three-way meeting.
